entries.description: Report an empirical association with its population or analytic scope attached.
entries.notes: Include direction, scale, uncertainty, and adjustment set where relevant.
entries.template: Within {scope}, {estimate} indicates an association between {variable_a} and {variable_b}.
entries.title: Report a scoped association

entries.description: Describe an adjusted association without implying that adjustment removes every source of bias.
entries.notes: Do not replace associated with affected, influenced, or caused.
entries.template: After adjustment for {covariates}, {finding} remained associated with {outcome}.
entries.title: Report adjusted association

entries.description: Describe a graded or dose-related observational pattern without assigning a causal mechanism.
entries.notes: A gradient can support but does not alone establish causation.
entries.template: Across {exposure_levels}, {pattern} was observed for {outcome}.
entries.title: Report a graded pattern

entries.description: Report predictive improvement against a benchmark without claiming explanation or intervention benefit.
entries.notes: Name the held-out population, horizon, metric, and uncertainty when available.
entries.template: In {evaluation_scope}, {estimate} shows that {predictor} improves prediction of {outcome} relative to {benchmark}.
entries.title: Separate prediction from explanation

entries.description: Keep a proposition attached to the source that advances it and to its stated boundary.
entries.notes: Retain the citation and do not present the attributed claim as an uncontested fact.
entries.template: According to {source}, {claim} within {scope}.
entries.title: Attribute a source claim

entries.description: Represent a source's interpretation together with the limitation it recognizes.
entries.notes: Replace source with a grammatical author reference and preserve the citation boundary.
entries.template: {source} interprets {evidence} as support for {claim}, while acknowledging {limitation}.
entries.title: Attribute an interpretation

entries.description: Introduce a source-specific definition without implying that it is the only accepted usage.
entries.notes: Preserve quotation marks when wording is copied exactly; otherwise paraphrase and cite.
entries.template: As {source} defines it, {term} refers to {definition}.
entries.title: Attribute a working definition

entries.description: Contrast two attributed positions while preserving ownership of each proposition.
entries.notes: Use parallel descriptions and avoid caricaturing either position.
entries.template: Where {source_a} treats {concept} as {position_a}, {source_b} treats it as {position_b}.
entries.title: Separate source positions

entries.description: State a causal effect from a randomized design while retaining its identifying assumptions.
entries.notes: Report assignment, adherence, estimand, uncertainty, and assumptions relevant to the effect.
entries.template: Under the randomized design and stated assumptions, {evidence} indicates that {cause} changed {outcome} by {estimate}.
entries.title: Randomized causal effect

entries.description: State a quasi-experimental causal estimate conditional on its central identifying assumption.
entries.notes: Pair with falsification, balance, sensitivity, or design-specific diagnostic evidence.
entries.template: If {identifying_assumption} holds, {estimate} estimates the effect of {cause} on {outcome}.
entries.title: Quasi-experimental causal estimate

entries.description: Express strengthened causal credibility from independent designs or evidence streams.
entries.notes: Explain how the evidence streams carry different biases and address the named alternative.
entries.template: Across {evidence}, the causal interpretation that {cause} affects {outcome} is more credible than {alternative}.
entries.title: Convergent causal inference

entries.description: Connect an intervention, a measured mechanism, and an outcome under a causal design.
entries.notes: A mechanism measurement alone does not establish mediation; report the identifying design.
entries.template: The intervention altered {mechanism}, and {evidence} supports a resulting change in {outcome}.
entries.title: Mechanism-linked causal claim

entries.description: Compare a shared direction while preserving a meaningful magnitude difference.
entries.notes: Ensure both results use compatible outcomes, scales, and comparison groups.
entries.template: Like {source}, {finding} shows {similarity}, although the magnitude differs by {difference}.
entries.title: Compare direction and magnitude

entries.description: Identify a specific dimension on which patterns from two contexts align.
entries.notes: Do not imply broader equivalence beyond the named dimension.
entries.template: The pattern in {context_a} parallels {finding} in {context_b} with respect to {dimension}.
entries.title: Compare across contexts

entries.description: Highlight outcome agreement across a specified methodological difference.
entries.notes: Methodological diversity strengthens convergence only when biases are not shared.
entries.template: Despite using {method_difference}, both analyses produced {finding}.
entries.title: Compare methods and outcomes

entries.description: Interpret an estimate against an explicit, relevant benchmark.
entries.notes: Justify why the selected benchmark is an appropriate reference point.
entries.template: Relative to {benchmark}, {estimate} represents {comparison} for {outcome}.
entries.title: Compare with a benchmark

entries.description: State a contrast while keeping source and present-study contexts visible.
entries.notes: Follow with design or context differences that could explain the contrast.
entries.template: Whereas {source} reports {finding}, the present analysis finds {result} in {scope}.
entries.title: Contrast by context

entries.description: Contrast how one observation relates to two specified theoretical predictions.
entries.notes: State each framework's prediction before judging alignment.
entries.template: {pattern} aligns with {framework_a} but differs from the prediction of {framework_b}.
entries.title: Contrast predictions

entries.description: Report a subgroup contrast without assuming the between-group difference is tested.
entries.notes: Add a formal interaction or contrast test before claiming that effects differ.
entries.template: The estimate for {group_a} was {estimate}, while the corresponding pattern for {group_b} was {pattern}.
entries.title: Contrast subgroup estimates

entries.description: Resolve or refine an apparent disagreement by identifying a relevant distinction.
entries.notes: The distinction should change what each claim entails, not merely rename the disagreement.
entries.template: The apparent conflict between {source} and {finding} narrows once {distinction} is made explicit.
entries.title: Separate apparent contradiction

entries.description: State a contribution through the specific gap, question, and scope it addresses.
entries.notes: Avoid first or novel unless a transparent search supports the priority claim.
entries.template: This study addresses {gap} by examining {question} in {scope}.
entries.title: Contribution to a bounded gap

entries.description: Describe a method, dataset, framework, or resource contribution without universal superiority claims.
entries.notes: State availability, validation, and scope separately when relevant.
entries.template: The study contributes {resource} for examining {question} under {condition}.
entries.title: Methodological contribution

entries.description: State an empirical contribution based on convergent evidence and a named scope.
entries.notes: Explain independence and relevance of the evidence streams before invoking convergence.
entries.template: By combining {evidence}, the study provides support for {claim} across {scope}.
entries.title: Empirical contribution from convergence

entries.description: State a conceptual contribution as a precise distinction rather than an unsupported novelty claim.
entries.notes: Show how the distinction changes analysis or interpretation, and cite prior formulations.
entries.template: The analysis refines {concept} by distinguishing {dimension_a} from {dimension_b}.
entries.title: Conceptual contribution

entries.description: Open a paper by locating a consequential problem inside an explicit setting or population.
entries.notes: Support consequential claims nearby and avoid implying universal importance.
entries.template: Within {scope}, {problem} remains consequential for {stakeholder}.
entries.title: Problem within a bounded setting

entries.description: Describe a bounded change in the emphasis of a literature without claiming complete consensus.
entries.notes: Define the reviewed literature and time boundary that support the stated shift.
entries.template: Recent work on {topic} has shifted attention from {earlier_focus} toward {current_focus}.
entries.title: Shift in scholarly attention

entries.description: Introduce an interpretive dispute through the conceptual distinction organizing it.
entries.notes: In part prevents the distinction from being presented as the debate's sole dimension.
entries.template: Debate about {concept} turns in part on how {distinction} is drawn.
entries.title: Frame an interpretive debate

entries.description: Frame an engineering or design problem as an explicit trade-off under a real constraint.
entries.notes: Verify that the objectives genuinely conflict in the defined operating context.
entries.template: For {system}, the practical challenge is to balance {objective_a} against {objective_b} under {constraint}.
entries.title: Frame an engineering trade-off

entries.description: Prevent a temporal sequence from being upgraded automatically to a causal relation.
entries.notes: State confounding, selection, reverse pathways, or design assumptions relevant to identification.
entries.template: Although {finding} establishes temporal order, it does not by itself identify {cause} as a cause of {outcome}.
entries.title: Temporal order is not causation

entries.description: Tie an observational interpretation to a specific unresolved source of confounding.
entries.notes: Do not imply that measured adjustment eliminates unmeasured or poorly measured confounding.
entries.template: Because {unmeasured_factor} may account for part of {finding}, {estimate} should be interpreted as associational.
entries.title: Bound residual confounding

entries.description: Separate predictive usefulness from a counterfactual intervention claim.
entries.notes: A causal claim needs an identified intervention, comparator, estimand, and assumptions.
entries.template: Although {result} improves prediction of {outcome}, it does not show that changing {predictor} would change that outcome.
entries.title: Prediction does not imply intervention effect

entries.description: Describe mechanism-compatible evidence without declaring a mediated causal pathway.
entries.notes: Mechanism measurement and temporal order alone do not identify mediation.
entries.template: The observed change in {mechanism} is compatible with mediation, but {evidence} does not isolate that pathway from {alternative}.
entries.title: Mediation remains unestablished

entries.description: Introduce a quantitative or qualitative result with outcome and scope attached.
entries.notes: Include units, uncertainty, and comparison basis where relevant.
entries.template: The analysis yielded {result} for {outcome} in {scope}.
entries.title: Report a measured result

entries.description: Attribute evidence and its intended proposition without adopting the source's conclusion automatically.
entries.notes: Use a precise source locator in the citation system required by the venue.
entries.template: In {source}, {evidence} is presented as evidence for {proposition}.
entries.title: Attribute source evidence

entries.description: Report a recurring empirical pattern while keeping its domain explicit.
entries.notes: Describe exceptions or heterogeneity immediately after the broad pattern when material.
entries.template: Across {scope}, the observed pattern was {pattern}.
entries.title: Present an observed pattern

entries.description: Report a point estimate together with its stated uncertainty interval.
entries.notes: Name the interval type and level in nearby text or notation.
entries.template: The estimate was {estimate}, with an uncertainty interval of {interval}.
entries.title: Introduce an uncertainty interval

entries.description: Identify a specific evidence gap without claiming that no work exists.
entries.notes: Support the gap with a transparent search or review boundary.
entries.template: The available {evidence} remains limited for {question} in {scope}.
entries.title: Bounded empirical gap

entries.description: Separate evidence for an observed pattern from uncertainty about its mechanism.
entries.notes: Do not imply that a mechanism is absent merely because it has not been established.
entries.template: Prior findings describe {pattern}, but the mechanism linking it to {outcome} remains unresolved.
entries.title: Unresolved mechanism gap

entries.description: Identify a construct or measurement dimension that current instruments underrepresent.
entries.notes: Ground the distinction between dimensions in theory or validation evidence.
entries.template: Existing measures capture {covered_dimension}, yet provide limited evidence about {missing_dimension}.
entries.title: Measurement gap

entries.description: Frame an open generalizability question as a change in a named condition.
entries.notes: Choose a condition with a reasoned basis for effect modification.
entries.template: It is not yet clear whether {finding} holds when {condition} changes.
entries.title: Boundary-condition gap

entries.description: Interpret a finding as support for a claim inside a named boundary.
entries.notes: Use indicates only when the design directly bears on the claim; otherwise select a tentative template.
entries.template: Within {scope}, {finding} indicates that {claim}.
entries.title: Bounded evidence interpretation

entries.description: Offer a tentative mechanism that could account for an observed finding.
entries.notes: Present competing mechanisms when the evidence cannot discriminate among them.
entries.template: One interpretation of {finding} is that {mechanism} may shape {outcome}.
entries.title: Mechanism-compatible interpretation

entries.description: Translate an estimate into a decision-relevant magnitude for a named stakeholder.
entries.notes: Keep the translation numerically traceable and separate it from value judgments.
entries.template: In practical terms, {estimate} corresponds to {real_world_meaning} for {stakeholder}.
entries.title: Practical magnitude interpretation

entries.description: Interpret an inconclusive result without equating non-significance with equivalence.
entries.notes: State the precision criterion or interval that leaves both possibilities open.
entries.template: Because {result} remains imprecise, the evidence does not distinguish between {possibility_a} and {possibility_b}.
entries.title: Null-compatible interpretation

entries.description: Justify a method through its fit with the research question and unit of analysis.
entries.notes: Directly addresses means fit to the question, not proof that the method is uniquely best.
entries.template: We chose {method} because it directly addresses {question} at the level of {unit}.
entries.title: Align method with question

entries.description: Explain the complementary contribution of two methods without assuming convergence in advance.
entries.notes: Do not claim validation merely because two methods were used.
entries.template: Combining {method_a} with {method_b} allows {aspect_a} and {aspect_b} to be examined separately.
entries.title: Justify triangulation

entries.description: Connect a sensitivity analysis to the assumption or analytic choice it probes.
entries.notes: Specify the plausible range and why it addresses the relevant uncertainty.
entries.template: We varied {assumption} to assess whether {claim} depended on {uncertain_choice}.
entries.title: Justify sensitivity analysis

entries.description: Explain how a corpus boundary enables a valid or interpretable comparison.
entries.notes: Also disclose what the boundary excludes and how that limits interpretation.
entries.template: The corpus was limited to {scope} so that {feature} could be compared under {shared_condition}.
entries.title: Justify corpus boundaries

entries.description: Connect a sampling boundary directly to the supported target population.
entries.notes: Avoid implying how the result would change in the excluded group without evidence.
entries.template: Because the sample excludes {excluded_group}, {finding} should be generalized only to {scope}.
entries.title: Sampling limitation

entries.description: Specify which construct dimension a measure captures and what it may miss.
entries.notes: Describe likely direction of bias only when supported.
entries.template: The measure captures {construct} through {indicator}, which may omit {uncaptured_dimension}.
entries.title: Measurement limitation

entries.description: Explain why a design cannot support causal interpretation of a finding.
entries.notes: Name the specific alternative causal pathway or bias left open.
entries.template: Since {design_feature} does not rule out {alternative}, {finding} should not be read as causal evidence.
entries.title: Design limitation on causality

entries.description: Tie limited precision to the range of interpretations still supported.
entries.notes: Report the interval or sensitivity range that motivates the statement.
entries.template: The wide uncertainty around {estimate} leaves both {interpretation_a} and {interpretation_b} compatible with {result}.
entries.title: Precision limitation

entries.description: Report the target group, sampling approach, and collection period without implying representativeness.
entries.notes: Describe eligibility, exclusions, recruitment, and response where relevant.
entries.template: We selected {population} using {sampling_method} during {period}.
entries.title: Describe sample selection

entries.description: State a quantitative model, outcome, and predictor set while marking prespecification accurately.
entries.notes: Remove prespecified unless the predictor set was fixed before the relevant analysis.
entries.template: We estimated {model} with {outcome} as the outcome and {predictors} as prespecified predictors.
entries.title: Describe a quantitative model

entries.description: Report qualitative material, analytic approach, and the iterative development of interpretation.
entries.notes: Describe researcher roles, reflexivity, disagreement handling, and software where relevant.
entries.template: We analyzed {material} using {analytic_approach}, iteratively refining {coding_framework}.
entries.title: Describe qualitative analysis

entries.description: Report the evaluated system, comparison benchmark, metric, and operating condition.
entries.notes: State dataset partitions, repetitions, hardware, and uncertainty when they affect comparability.
entries.template: We evaluated {system} against {benchmark} using {metric} under {condition}.
entries.title: Describe system evaluation

entries.description: Report a threshold-based null result while retaining what the uncertainty interval permits.
entries.notes: Give the estimate, interval, threshold, and analysis context; do not conclude no effect.
entries.template: For {outcome}, {result} did not meet {decision_threshold}; the interval remained compatible with {possibility}.
entries.title: Report threshold and interval

entries.description: State an equivalence conclusion only from an analysis and margin designed for that purpose.
entries.notes: Use only when the margin was justified and the analysis satisfies its assumptions.
entries.template: The equivalence analysis yielded {result}, supporting equivalence within the prespecified margin of {margin}.
entries.title: Report equivalence result

entries.description: Explain that an estimate leaves a substantive question unresolved because precision is limited.
entries.notes: State the interval or sensitivity range showing why the question remains unresolved.
entries.template: Across {scope}, {estimate} was too imprecise to resolve whether {claim}.
entries.title: Report unresolved imprecision

entries.description: Report that an event was not observed while preventing an unsupported universal absence claim.
entries.notes: Consider detection limits, sample size, search strategy, and opportunities for observation.
entries.template: No instances of {phenomenon} were observed in {scope}; this {result} does not establish absence beyond that scope.
entries.title: Bound an absence observation

entries.description: Signal that a source proposition is being paraphrased and connected to the current argument.
entries.notes: Draft independently from semantic notes, preserve the citation, and avoid close structural imitation.
entries.template: {source} argues that {claim}; here, that position is restated in relation to {current_focus}.
entries.title: Restate a source proposition

entries.description: Retain attribution when a current argument adopts or develops a source's conceptual distinction.
entries.notes: Clarify which part comes from the source and which part is the current writer's development.
entries.template: Building on {source}, the present account distinguishes {concept_a} from {concept_b}.
entries.title: Build on an attributed distinction

entries.description: Provide an attributed summary of a source's mechanism without adopting it as established fact.
entries.notes: Preserve qualifications and causal status; quote instead if distinctive wording is indispensable.
entries.template: The mechanism proposed in {source} can be summarized as {summary}.
entries.title: Summarize a proposed mechanism

entries.description: Make explicit that expression changes while the attributed proposition remains source-dependent.
entries.notes: This pattern does not remove citation duties and should not be used to disguise copied expression.
entries.template: Without reproducing {source}'s wording, this account retains its proposition that {claim}.
entries.title: Mark proposition preservation

entries.description: State the central position while naming the boundary within which it applies.
entries.notes: Replace scope with a population, setting, corpus, period, or analytic boundary.
entries.template: This study argues that {claim} within {scope}.
entries.title: Direct scoped position

entries.description: Choose a bounded position after presenting a relevant empirical finding.
entries.notes: The claim must remain within what the stated finding can distinguish.
entries.template: Given {finding}, the more defensible interpretation is that {claim}.
entries.title: Position from observed result

entries.description: Locate a proposition inside a named theoretical or conceptual framework.
entries.notes: Clarify whether the framework guides interpretation or is itself being tested.
entries.template: Using {framework} as the analytic lens, we propose that {claim}.
entries.title: Theory-guided proposition

entries.description: State a position supported by multiple independent and mutually relevant lines of evidence.
entries.notes: Name the independent lines of evidence instead of using convergence as decoration.
entries.template: Taken together, {evidence} supports the position that {claim}.
entries.title: Convergent position

entries.description: Report a recurring pattern across qualitative materials while retaining its evidential source.
entries.notes: Describe variation and show how the pattern was developed from the material.
entries.template: Across {source}, {pattern} recurred in accounts of {experience}.
entries.title: Interpret a recurring qualitative pattern

entries.description: Interpret a common qualitative finding while preserving a counterexample or deviant case.
entries.notes: Do not reduce frequency to prevalence unless the design supports quantitative inference.
entries.template: {finding} was common, but {counterexample} shows that it was not uniform across {scope}.
entries.title: Retain a deviant case

entries.description: Offer an interpretation grounded in qualitative evidence while keeping an alternative account live.
entries.notes: Make the link between evidence and interpretation explicit rather than relying on suggests alone.
entries.template: {evidence} suggests {claim}, although {alternative} remains plausible.
entries.title: Offer a bounded qualitative interpretation

entries.description: Connect researcher position or access to a bounded interpretation of qualitative material.
entries.notes: Be specific about access, relationship, or analytic standpoint; avoid generic reflexivity claims.
entries.template: Because {researcher_position} shaped access to {material}, {finding} is interpreted within {scope}.
entries.title: Locate interpretation reflexively

entries.description: Mark an interpretation as plausible while explicitly withholding certainty.
entries.notes: Keep evidence wording concrete nearby; this sentence is not a substitute for describing it.
entries.template: The available evidence, {evidence}, suggests but does not establish that {claim}.
entries.title: Confidence qualifier

entries.description: Prevent overgeneralization by naming both the supported scope and an excluded context.
entries.notes: Choose an excluded context that differs on a theoretically relevant dimension.
entries.template: This claim is limited to {scope} and may not extend to {excluded_context}.
entries.title: Boundary qualifier

entries.description: Make the premise needed for an empirical interpretation visible.
entries.notes: State a checkable condition; avoid conditions that merely restate the claim.
entries.template: If {condition} holds, {finding} is consistent with {claim}.
entries.title: Conditional interpretation

entries.description: Acknowledge a live alternative explanation when evidence is not uniquely diagnostic.
entries.notes: Use only when the alternative could plausibly generate the stated finding.
entries.template: Although {finding} supports {claim}, it remains compatible with {alternative}.
entries.title: Alternative-compatible claim

entries.description: Turn a bounded research gap into a specific, testable next study.
entries.notes: Explain how the proposed method addresses the identified limitation or gap.
entries.template: Future work should test {question} in {scope} using {method}.
entries.title: Research recommendation from gap

entries.description: Offer a reversible, conditional practice option with an explicit monitoring target.
entries.notes: Use could consider when benefits and harms remain uncertain; state trade-offs nearby.
entries.template: Given {evidence}, where {condition} applies, {stakeholder} could consider {action} while monitoring {outcome}.
entries.title: Conditional practice recommendation

entries.description: Recommend bounded implementation backed by direct evidence and a review point.
entries.notes: Assess feasibility, distributional effects, harms, and stakeholder values before use.
entries.template: Given {evidence}, implementation of {action} is warranted for {scope}, with review after {timeframe}.
entries.title: Evidence-backed implementation recommendation

entries.description: Recommend a limited next step that also reduces consequential uncertainty.
entries.notes: Prefer reversible actions when downside risk or evidential uncertainty is high.
entries.template: Until {uncertainty} is resolved, a proportionate step is to {action} and collect {evidence}.
entries.title: Decision under uncertainty

entries.description: Acknowledge a concrete review point and state the corresponding manuscript revision.
entries.notes: Describe the change precisely; do not claim resolution when the concern remains partly open.
entries.template: We thank the reviewer for identifying {issue}; we revised {location} to {revision}.
entries.title: Acknowledge and revise

entries.description: Explain a reasoned disagreement with a reviewer while adding a clarifying boundary.
entries.notes: Address the strongest version of the concern and keep tone factual rather than defensive.
entries.template: We respectfully retain {decision} because {reason}; the manuscript now clarifies {boundary}.
entries.title: Respectfully retain a decision

entries.description: Connect a review comment to a new analysis, its result, and its manuscript location.
entries.notes: Do not imply that the added analysis validates claims beyond its design and assumptions.
entries.template: In response to {comment}, we added {analysis}; {result} is now reported in {location}.
entries.title: Report added analysis

entries.description: Accept a valid limitation and show where its consequence for a claim is disclosed.
entries.notes: The revised manuscript should state the inferential consequence, not merely name the limitation.
entries.template: We agree that {limitation} constrains {claim}; this is now stated in {location}.
entries.title: Acknowledge a limitation

entries.description: Define the population, setting, and period covered by an analysis.
entries.notes: Use the same boundary terms consistently in methods, results, and conclusions.
entries.template: The analysis concerns {population} in {setting} during {period}.
entries.title: Population and setting scope

entries.description: Define a term operationally and name a nearby meaning that is excluded.
entries.notes: Do not present a stipulative definition as universal usage.
entries.template: Here, {term} refers specifically to {definition}, excluding {excluded_meaning}.
entries.title: Conceptual definition scope

entries.description: Set the unit of analysis and an explicit non-goal.
entries.notes: Check that later claims do not shift to a different unit without justification.
entries.template: This analysis evaluates {outcome} at the {unit} level and does not address {outside_scope}.
entries.title: Analytic boundary

entries.description: State the source type, inclusion criterion, and temporal cutoff of a review.
entries.notes: Report databases, languages, screening process, and exclusions elsewhere in the method.
entries.template: The review includes {source} that meet {criterion} and were available by {date}.
entries.title: Review inclusion boundary

entries.description: Integrate multiple independent sources around a conditional shared proposition.
entries.notes: Use plural source wording in the filled slot and identify meaningful disagreement separately.
entries.template: Across {source}, {evidence} converges on {claim}, particularly under {condition}.
entries.title: Synthesize shared proposition

entries.description: Combine sources that illuminate different parts of the same problem.
entries.notes: Explain the link between the two aspects in the next sentence.
entries.template: Together, {source_a} explains {aspect_a}, while {source_b} clarifies {aspect_b}.
entries.title: Synthesize complementary roles

entries.description: Synthesize disagreement by organizing sources around a clearly posed question.
entries.notes: Represent each position charitably and include mixed or intermediate accounts when relevant.
entries.template: The literature divides over {question}: {source_a} supports {position_a}, whereas {source_b} supports {position_b}.
entries.title: Map a structured disagreement

entries.description: Distinguish direct support from contextual material within a synthesis.
entries.notes: Explain the criteria used to rank evidential strength.
entries.template: The strongest support for {claim} comes from {evidence}, while {source} supplies contextual detail.
entries.title: Synthesize evidence hierarchy

entries.description: Report an estimate together with the endpoints of its stated uncertainty interval.
entries.notes: State interval type, level, scale, and units; preserve endpoint signs and precision.
entries.template: For {outcome}, {estimate} was accompanied by an uncertainty interval from {lower_bound} to {upper_bound}.
entries.title: Report estimate and interval

entries.description: Summarize how an estimate varies across prespecified or justified sensitivity analyses.
entries.notes: Name the varied assumptions; a narrow range does not address biases shared by all analyses.
entries.template: Across the sensitivity analyses, {estimate} ranged from {lower_result} to {upper_result}.
entries.title: Report sensitivity range

entries.description: Locate imprecision in a subgroup and state the substantive possibilities it leaves open.
entries.notes: Avoid treating subgroup estimates as different without a relevant contrast or interaction test.
entries.template: Uncertainty was greatest for {subgroup}, where {result} remained compatible with {possibilities}.
entries.title: Report heterogeneous uncertainty

entries.description: Connect a known measurement limitation to the boundary on an empirical estimate.
entries.notes: State direction or magnitude of measurement error only when evidence supports it.
entries.template: Because {measurement_issue} affects {estimate}, the reported value should be read within {uncertainty_boundary}.
entries.title: Bound measurement uncertainty
